--- ABSTRACT ---
[CONTEXT]: Papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) is the most common endocrine malignancy. It has been demonstrated that micro-RNAs (miRNAs) are involved in the development of PTC. The miRNA-chromatin immunoprecipitation microarray assay revealed down-regulation of miR-219-5p; however, the effect of miR-219-5p on PTC cell growth remains unknown. This result implied the critical role of miR-219-5p in the development of PTC.
[METHODS]: We investigated the association between miR-219-5p and PTC development. Expression of miR-219-5p was monitored in 30 PTC tissue specimens and compared with that in 30 normal thyroid tissue specimens. The effect of miR-219-5p on PTC development was studied by cell proliferation, migration, and apoptosis assays. The underlying mechanism was clarified by a reporter assay and rescue experiment.
[RESULTS]: The current study confirmed that miR-219-5p expression was inhibited in PTC tissue samples. There were statistically significant differences in the expression of miR-219-5p with regard to sex, tumor size, and lymph node metastasis in patients with PTC. Forced expression of miR-219-5p suppressed PTC cell proliferation and migration and promoted apoptosis. Further study showed that estrogen receptor (ER) α was the direct target of miR-219-5p and mediated the effect of miR-219-5p on PTC occurrence. Expression of miR-219-5p was inversely correlated with that of ERα. Importantly, ERα overexpression in PTC cells rescued the inhibitory effect of miR-219-5p on PTC cell proliferation and migration. Thus, our results indicated that miR-219-5p played a critical role in PTC growth by inhibiting ERα.
[CONCLUSION]: Our investigation identified miR-219-5p as a negative regulator of PTC development through targeting of ERα.

key_findings.finding: A direct primary study exists: PMID 25423566, “miR-219-5p modulates cell growth of papillary thyroid carcinoma by targeting estrogen receptor α” (J Clin Endocrinol Metab, 2015). In 30 PTC and 30 normal thyroid specimens, miR-219-5p was reduced in PTC; forced miR-219-5p expression suppressed PTC-cell proliferation and migration and increased apoptosis. The abstract explicitly states that ERα/ESR1 was the direct target, with an underlying reporter assay and rescue experiment, and that ERα overexpression rescued the miR-219-5p-mediated inhibition of proliferation and migration.

source_tools.relevance: PubMed abstract and extracted paper content directly report the study design and findings, including proliferation, migration, apoptosis, reporter assay, and rescue.
Exact PubMed title, PMID, journal/year, and matching miR-219-5p/PTC/ERα result.

key_findings.finding: The evidence meets the requested functional-target standard at the abstract level: the paper reports a reporter assay (consistent with direct 3′UTR validation) plus ERα overexpression rescue, and links ERα expression inversely to miR-219-5p. However, the available PubMed record/abstract does not specify the exact PTC cell-line names or provide the reporter construct details, luciferase mutant-versus-wild-type results, or assay-level expression values; full text was not available through the retrieval source.

source_tools.relevance: Content retrieval explicitly states full text was unavailable and supplies only the abstract, while the abstract confirms reporter assay and rescue.
PubTator annotation independently links PMID 25423566 to PTC and ESR1.

key_findings.finding: No second PubMed primary study was identified that independently tests the exact miR-219-5p + PTC + ESR1/ERα combination; other retrieved records were reviews, bioinformatics/network papers, or studies of miR-219-5p in non-thyroid cancers. Thus PMID 25423566 is the closest—and apparently the direct—evidence rather than merely an insufficient indirect study.

source_tools.relevance: Exact-phrase and PTC proliferation searches returned PMID 25423566 as the uniquely matching primary study; remaining results were reviews, non-PTC studies, or unrelated network analyses.
Broader miR-219-5p thyroid search showed mainly reviews/network studies and no additional matching ESR1 functional paper.
